/aerospace-engineering/aircraft-material.alt: Top view schematic of a conventional airliner showing typical material zones: fuselage skin in 2024 aluminium, upper wing skin in 7075 aluminium, lower wing skin in 2024 aluminium, engine pylons and main landing gear fittings in titanium, and flaps, ailerons and tail surfaces in carbon fibre composite, with a colour legend

/aerospace-engineering/aircraft-structur.alt: Exploded schematic of an aircraft: fuselage with frames and stringers, wing with front and rear spars and ribs forming a wing box, empennage with horizontal and vertical stabilisers, landing gear, and engine nacelle under the wing; labels for each component

/aerospace-engineering/avionics-systems-.alt: Avionics architecture: sensors such as air data computer, inertial reference unit, GNSS receiver, radio navigation and radar feed a data network; flight management and flight control computers process the data; cockpit displays and controls show information to the crew; communication and surveillance radios connect to air traffic control and other aircraft; actuators move control surfaces

/aerospace-engineering/drag-force-on-air.alt: Graph of drag force against airspeed for a light aircraft: parasite drag curve rising with speed squared, induced drag curve falling with speed, and the total drag curve forming a U shape with its minimum where parasite and induced drag are equal, at about 39 metres per second

/aerospace-engineering/forces-of-flight-.alt: Side view of an aircraft in level flight with four force arrows: lift pointing up from the wing, weight pointing down from the centre of gravity, thrust pointing forward from the engine and drag pointing backward

/aerospace-engineering/how-a-quadcopter-.alt: Top view of an X configuration quadcopter: four arms with motors and propellers at the corners, front left and rear right spinning counterclockwise, front right and rear left spinning clockwise; central body contains flight controller, battery, ESCs and GPS; arrow indicates front

/aerospace-engineering/how-wings-generat.alt: Airfoil at a positive angle of attack in airflow: streamlines approach from the left, curve over the upper surface and leave the trailing edge deflected downward; low pressure region above the airfoil marked with minus signs, higher pressure below marked with plus signs; lift arrow perpendicular to the relative wind and drag arrow parallel to it; chord line and angle of attack shown

/aerospace-engineering/satellite-subsyst.alt: Satellite block diagram: central bus box containing onboard computer connected to power, thermal, ADCS, propulsion and TT&C subsystems, plus the payload; solar arrays on both sides, antenna on top, star tracker and thrusters indicated

/aerospace-engineering/turbojet-vs-turbo.alt: Three engine schematics stacked: turbojet with compressor, combustor, turbine and narrow hot jet; turbofan with large front fan, bypass duct around the core and two exhaust streams; turboprop with propeller driven through a reduction gearbox by the core turbine and a small exhaust

/agricultural-engineering/automated-irri.alt: Closed loop irrigation control: soil moisture sensors at two depths in the root zone send signals to a controller; the controller also receives rain and weather data and flow meter feedback; it commands the pump and solenoid valve which supply the drip lines; a cloud dashboard allows remote monitoring

/agricultural-engineering/cold-storage-d.alt: Cold room cross section showing heat gains: transmission through insulated walls, roof and floor; infiltration through the door; product heat and respiration from stacked produce; internal loads from lights, people and evaporator fans; the evaporator unit cooler inside removes heat and the condensing unit outside rejects it

/agricultural-engineering/combine-harves.alt: Side view of a conventional combine harvester moving to the left: the reel sweeps crop onto the cutterbar, the header auger and feeder chain carry it up to the threshing cylinder and concave, straw passes rearward over the straw walkers and leaves at the back, threshed grain falls onto the grain pan and sieves where fan air blows chaff out of the rear, and clean grain is carried by the clean grain auger and elevator up into the grain tank

/agricultural-engineering/drip-vs-sprink.alt: Two layouts compared. Left: drip system with pump, screen or disc filter, fertiliser injector, main line, sub-main and laterals with emitters beside each plant, wetting only small bulbs of soil around the roots. Right: sprinkler system with pump, main line, lateral and risers with sprinklers spraying overlapping circles covering the whole field

/agricultural-engineering/grain-drying-m.alt: Continuous cross flow grain dryer: wet grain enters at the top and flows downward by gravity between two perforated columns; heated air from a burner and fan blows across the grain columns in the heating section; ambient air cools grain in the lower section; dry cool grain exits at the bottom through a metering roll; moist exhaust air leaves through the outside of the columns

/agricultural-engineering/haccp-principl.alt: Twelve HACCP steps in two columns: five preliminary steps (assemble team, describe product, identify intended use, construct flow diagram, verify flow diagram on site) followed by the seven principles (hazard analysis, determine CCPs, critical limits, monitoring, corrective actions, verification, records)

/agricultural-engineering/irrigation-wat.alt: Crop coefficient curve for grain maize over the season: flat Kc initial of 0.30 during the initial stage, a straight rise during crop development, a flat Kc mid of 1.20 in mid-season, and a decline to Kc end of 0.35 to 0.60 during the late season stage

/agricultural-engineering/pasteurization.alt: HTST pasteurizer flow: raw milk at 4 degrees from the balance tank passes through the regeneration section (raw side) where it is preheated, then the heating section to 72 degrees, then the holding tube for 15 seconds, then the flow diversion valve; correctly heated milk flows back through the regeneration section (pasteurized side) where it gives up heat, then the cooling section to 4 degrees and to the filler; under-temperature milk is diverted back to the balance tank

/agricultural-engineering/precision-agri.alt: Precision agriculture cycle with four stages in a loop: collect data (GNSS, yield monitor, soil samples, satellites, drones, sensors), analyse and map (GIS, zones, prescriptions), apply variably (auto-steer, variable rate seeding, fertiliser, spraying, irrigation), evaluate results (yield maps, records), then back to collect

/agricultural-engineering/tractor-power-.alt: Block diagram of tractor power flow: engine to clutch to gearbox, then to bevel gear and differential, then to final drive reduction gears on each side and the rear wheels; a separate shaft from the clutch or gearbox drives the PTO at the rear, and the engine also drives the hydraulic pump

/ai-data-engineering/big-data-five-vs/.alt: Big data shown as a central circle surrounded by five circles: volume (scale of data), velocity (speed of arrival), variety (formats and sources), veracity (quality and trust) and value (business insight)

/ai-data-engineering/classification-vs-d.alt: Three panels of the same scene with a car and a person. Panel one, classification, shows a single label for the whole image. Panel two, detection, shows a bounding box around the car and another around the person. Panel three, segmentation, shows the car and person filled with coloured pixel masks

/ai-data-engineering/convolutional-neura.alt: A 3 by 3 kernel slides across a 5 by 5 input with stride 1, producing a 3 by 3 feature map; three kernel positions along the top row map to the three top cells of the feature map; below, a CNN pipeline: input, convolution with ReLU, pooling, convolution with ReLU, pooling, dense layer, softmax output

/ai-data-engineering/data-science-workfl.alt: Data science workflow as eight connected steps in a loop: define problem, collect data, clean and prepare, explore, feature engineering, model, evaluate, deploy and monitor, with a feedback arrow back to define problem

/ai-data-engineering/etl-vs-elt/.alt: Top row ETL: sources, then extract to a separate transform server, then load into the data warehouse. Bottom row ELT: sources, then extract and load raw data directly into the warehouse, where transformation happens inside the warehouse

/ai-data-engineering/how-large-language-.alt: LLM generation loop: input tokens go to embeddings, then through a stack of transformer layers with attention and feedforward blocks, then to output probabilities over the vocabulary; the chosen next token is appended to the input and the loop repeats

/ai-data-engineering/how-neural-networks.alt: Feedforward neural network with an input layer of three neurons, two hidden layers of four neurons each, and an output layer of two neurons; every neuron connects to every neuron in the next layer

/ai-data-engineering/overfitting-and-und.alt: Error against model complexity. Training error falls steadily as complexity increases. Validation error falls, reaches a minimum at the best fit, then rises. The left region is underfitting with high bias and the right region is overfitting with high variance.

/ai-data-engineering/predictive-maintena.alt: Predictive maintenance pipeline: sensors on a motor and pump send data to data collection, then feature extraction, then machine learning models, then maintenance action in the CMMS, with feedback from maintenance records to the models

/ai-data-engineering/supervised-vs-unsup.alt: Left: supervised learning plot with labelled points of two classes, circles and triangles, separated by a learned decision boundary. Right: unsupervised learning plot with unlabelled points forming three clusters found by the algorithm

/ai-data-engineering/tokenization-and-em.alt: Pipeline: input text 'Pumps overheat' is split into subword tokens Pump, s, over, heat; each token maps to an integer ID; each ID looks up a row in the embedding matrix to give a dense vector of numbers

/automation-robotics/dcs-architecture/.alt: DCS architecture: operator stations, engineering station and historian on a redundant plant control network at the top; redundant controller pairs in the middle each with I/O modules; field instruments and control valves at the bottom; a separate safety system alongside

/automation-robotics/digital-twin-explai.alt: Digital twin data loop: a physical asset with sensors sends data through connectivity to the digital twin, which contains models, simulation and analytics; the twin returns insights, predictions and optimised settings to operators and to the control system of the physical asset

/automation-robotics/hmi-design-best-pra.alt: HMI display hierarchy as a four level pyramid: Level 1 area overview at the top, Level 2 process unit control, Level 3 process unit detail, and Level 4 support and diagnostic displays at the base; an arrow on the left shows navigation from overview down to detail

/automation-robotics/machine-vision-comp.alt: Machine vision setup: a part on a conveyor lit by a ring light, a camera with lens above it, a trigger sensor beside the conveyor, a vision processor receiving images, and a PLC receiving pass or fail results that drives a reject device

/automation-robotics/mechatronic-system-.alt: Mechatronic system block diagram: a set point enters the controller, which drives an actuator through a power amplifier; the actuator moves the mechanical system; a sensor measures the output and feeds it back through signal conditioning to the controller

/automation-robotics/modbus-rtu-vs-tcp/.alt: Frame comparison: a Modbus RTU frame with slave address, function code, data and CRC; and a Modbus TCP frame with a 7 byte MBAP header containing transaction ID, protocol ID, length and unit ID, followed by function code and data, carried inside a TCP/IP packet

/automation-robotics/plc-hardware-select.alt: Modular PLC on a rack: power supply module, CPU module with communication ports, digital input, digital output, analog input and analog output modules, connected to field sensors and actuators below and to an HMI or SCADA network above

/automation-robotics/plc-ladder-logic/.alt: Two ladder rungs. Rung 1: START contact in parallel with a motor M seal-in contact, in series with STOP and overload OL contacts, driving the MOTOR coil. Rung 2: M contact enabling an on delay timer TON T1 with preset 5 seconds, whose output drives the FAN coil.

/automation-robotics/scada-system-archit.alt: SCADA architecture in layers: at the top the control centre with operator HMI stations, SCADA servers and a historian; a communication network in the middle using fibre, radio or cellular links; local controllers such as PLCs and RTUs at remote sites; and field devices such as sensors, valves and pumps at the bottom

/automation-robotics/servo-vs-stepper-mo.alt: Top: open loop stepper system where a controller sends step and direction pulses to a driver that powers the stepper motor with no feedback. Bottom: closed loop servo system where a controller sends a command to a servo drive that powers the motor, and an encoder on the motor feeds position back to the drive

/automation-robotics/types-of-industrial.alt: Simplified side views of four robot types: an articulated arm with rotary joints, a SCARA robot with two horizontal arms and a vertical quill, a Cartesian gantry with three linear axes, and a delta robot with three parallel arms carrying a small platform

/biomedical-engineering/biomaterials-typ.alt: Total hip replacement showing biomaterials: titanium alloy femoral stem in the femur, cobalt chromium or ceramic femoral head, UHMWPE liner inside a titanium acetabular cup in the pelvis, hydroxyapatite coating on the stem surface; labels for each material

/biomedical-engineering/biopotential-mea.alt: Biopotential measurement chain: two electrodes on the body connected to an instrumentation amplifier with a right leg drive electrode; amplifier output passes through high pass filter, low pass filter and 50 or 60 hertz notch filter, then isolation barrier, ADC and display; common mode interference from mains shown coupling to the body

/biomedical-engineering/bioreactor-types.alt: Stirred tank bioreactor: cylindrical vessel with cooling jacket, motor driven shaft with two Rushton turbine impellers, baffles on the walls, air sparger at the bottom producing bubbles, probes for pH, dissolved oxygen and temperature, feed, acid and base inlets, exhaust gas outlet with filter and harvest outlet at the bottom

/biomedical-engineering/how-mri-works/.alt: MRI scanner cross section and imaging sequence: concentric superconducting magnet, gradient coils and RF body coil around a patient on a table, a five step sequence of spin alignment in B0, RF excitation, precession inducing a signal, T1 and T2 relaxation and Fourier reconstruction, and a signal chain from receive coil to receiver and ADC, computer and image

/biomedical-engineering/medical-device-c.alt: Risk ladder comparing classification systems: from low to high risk, EU classes I, IIa, IIb, III; US FDA classes I, II, III; India classes A, B, C, D; examples at each level: bandages and stethoscopes, hearing aids and infusion sets, ventilators and bone screws, pacemakers and heart valves

/biomedical-engineering/medical-imaging-.alt: Four schematics: X-ray tube sending beam through patient to detector; CT with source and detector rotating around patient in a ring gantry; MRI with patient inside a cylindrical magnet with RF coil; ultrasound probe on skin sending pulses and receiving echoes from an organ

/biomedical-engineering/prosthetic-limbs.alt: Two transradial prostheses compared. Left: body-powered with a figure of eight harness across the shoulders, a control cable running along the arm to a split hook terminal device; shoulder movement pulls the cable to open the hook. Right: myoelectric with EMG electrodes inside the socket over residual muscles, a battery and controller in the forearm, and a motorised hand

/biomedical-engineering/pulse-oximeter-w.alt: Pulse oximeter block diagram: red 660 nanometre and infrared 940 nanometre LEDs shine through a finger onto a photodiode, which feeds a transimpedance amplifier, an ADC and processor, and a display of SpO2 and pulse rate. A plot shows the detected light signal with a large steady DC level and a small pulsatile AC component.

/biomedical-engineering/spectrophotomete.alt: Single beam spectrophotometer: light source emits white light through an entrance slit to a diffraction grating that disperses wavelengths; an exit slit selects one wavelength which passes through the sample cuvette with path length l; transmitted light of intensity I reaches the detector, connected to electronics and display showing absorbance

/chemical-engineering/cstr-vs-pfr/.alt: Left: a stirred tank reactor with feed in, an agitator and product out, uniform composition throughout. Right: a tubular plug flow reactor with concentration falling along its length from inlet to outlet

/chemical-engineering/distillation-colum.alt: Distillation column with trays; feed enters at the middle; vapour from the top goes to a condenser and reflux drum, part of the liquid returns as reflux and the rest leaves as distillate; liquid at the bottom goes to a reboiler which returns vapour to the column, and bottoms product leaves

/chemical-engineering/energy-balance/.alt: A dashed system boundary around a process unit. Feed streams with mass flow and specific enthalpy enter from the left, product streams leave on the right. Heat Q enters from below and shaft work Ws leaves from the top.

/chemical-engineering/filtration-equipme.alt: Rotary drum vacuum filter: a perforated drum covered with filter cloth rotates clockwise, partly submerged in a slurry trough; cake forms in the submerged zone, is washed by sprays and dried by air on the top of the drum, then removed by a scraper blade on the right side; filtrate and wash liquid are drawn through the drum centre to a vacuum receiver

/chemical-engineering/haber-bosch-ammoni.alt: Block flow diagram of an ammonia plant: natural gas and steam go to desulphurisation and reforming, with air added in the secondary reformer; then shift conversion, CO2 removal, methanation and compression feed the synthesis loop, where a converter, cooler and separator produce liquid ammonia while unreacted gas is recycled and a small purge is removed

/chemical-engineering/heat-exchanger-typ.alt: Shell and tube heat exchanger: tube side fluid enters the front channel head, flows through the tube bundle and leaves the rear head; shell side fluid enters the shell at the top left and zigzags across the tubes around segmental baffles before leaving at the bottom right

/chemical-engineering/material-balance/.alt: Mixer block with two inlet streams and one outlet: stream 1 is 100 kg/h of 20 percent NaOH solution, stream 2 is water of unknown flow, and stream 3 is the 5 percent NaOH product of unknown flow

/chemical-engineering/pfd-vs-pid/.alt: Left: a PFD of a tank feeding a pump with one stream number. Right: the same section as a P&ID with isolation valves, a level transmitter and level controller bubble, a control valve on the pump discharge and a line number

/chemical-engineering/pinch-analysis/.alt: Temperature against enthalpy plot with a hot composite curve above a cold composite curve; they overlap in the middle where heat is recovered, approach most closely at the pinch separated by delta T min, the cold curve extends beyond the hot curve on the right showing minimum hot utility, and the hot curve extends beyond the cold curve on the left showing minimum cold utility

/chemical-engineering/pressure-vessels-b.alt: Horizontal pressure vessel with cylindrical shell, ellipsoidal heads at both ends, inlet and outlet nozzles on top, a manway, a drain nozzle at the bottom and two saddle supports

/chemical-engineering/size-reduction-equ.alt: Jaw crusher: a fixed jaw on the left and a swinging jaw on the right driven by an eccentric shaft form a V shaped chamber; large feed lumps enter at the top and crushed product leaves through the narrow discharge gap at the bottom

/civil-engineering/bearing-capacity-of-s.alt: General shear failure under a strip footing: a wedge of soil under the footing moves down, radial shear zones on each side, and passive zones pushing soil up beside the footing at the ground surface

/civil-engineering/flexible-vs-rigid-pav.alt: Side by side cross sections: a flexible pavement with bituminous surface, base, sub-base and subgrade, where wheel load spreads in a narrow cone; and a rigid pavement with concrete slab and dry lean concrete over subgrade, where load spreads over a wide area

/civil-engineering/levelling-in-surveyin.alt: Levelling setup: an automatic level on a tripod between two staffs; the horizontal line of sight cuts the backsight staff on the benchmark and the foresight staff on point A, which is lower on sloping ground

/civil-engineering/limit-state-design-rc.alt: Rectangular RCC beam section with tension bars at the bottom, the linear strain diagram with 0.0035 at the top, and the equivalent stress block giving compression force 0.36 fck b xu at 0.42 xu from the top and tension force 0.87 fy Ast in the steel

/civil-engineering/quantity-estimation-m.alt: Plan of a two room building with an internal partition wall; centre lines of walls are dashed; the two T junctions where the partition meets the long walls are marked; dimensions 8 m by 4 m centre to centre

/civil-engineering/shear-force-and-bendi.alt: Simply supported beam with a uniformly distributed load; the shear force diagram falls linearly from plus wL over 2 at the left support to minus wL over 2 at the right support, and the bending moment diagram is a parabola with maximum wL squared over 8 at midspan

/civil-engineering/steel-sections-types/.alt: Cross sections of six common steel shapes: I-beam, H column section, channel, equal angle, tee and square and circular hollow sections

/civil-engineering/types-of-beams/.alt: Four beam types. Top left: simply supported beam with a pin at the left and a roller at the right. Top right: cantilever beam fixed into a wall at the left and free at the right. Bottom left: overhanging beam on a pin and a roller with one end extending beyond the roller. Bottom right: fixed beam built into walls at both ends.

/civil-engineering/types-of-bridges/.alt: Six bridge forms drawn as simple elevations: beam bridge on two piers, truss bridge with triangulated members, arch bridge with curved arch under the deck, cantilever bridge with arms meeting at midspan, suspension bridge with sagging main cable and vertical hangers, and cable-stayed bridge with straight cables from towers to deck

/civil-engineering/types-of-cement/.alt: Classification of cement types into three groups: ordinary Portland cement in 33, 43 and 53 grades; blended cements PPC, PSC and composite; special cements such as sulphate resisting, rapid hardening, low heat, white and masonry cement

/civil-engineering/types-of-foundations/.alt: Cross sections of three types of foundations: an isolated footing under one column in firm soil, a raft slab under several columns on weak soil, and a pile foundation where a pile cap on piles passes through soft soil to a hard stratum.

/civil-engineering/water-cement-ratio/.alt: Graph of concrete compressive strength against water cement ratio: strength falls steadily as the ratio increases for fully compacted concrete; at very low ratios with poor compaction the strength drops away

/computer-science/arrays-vs-linked-lists.alt: Top: an array of five elements stored in adjacent memory cells with indices 0 to 4. Bottom: a singly linked list of four nodes scattered in memory, each node holding a value and a pointer to the next node, with the last pointer null

/computer-science/big-o-notation/.alt: Graph of number of operations against input size n for common complexity classes: O(1) flat, O(log n) slowly rising, O(n) straight line, O(n log n) slightly steeper, and O(n squared) rising steeply

/computer-science/compiled-vs-interprete.alt: Three paths from source code: a compiler producing a native executable that runs on the CPU; an interpreter that reads source and executes it directly; and a bytecode compiler feeding a virtual machine that interprets bytecode and JIT compiles hot code

/computer-science/database-normalization.alt: Normalized design with four tables: Student with StudentID and StudentName; Enrolment with StudentID and CourseID as composite key; Course with CourseID, CourseTitle and InstructorID; Instructor with InstructorID, Name and Phone; lines show foreign keys from Enrolment to Student and Course, and from Course to Instructor

/computer-science/how-http-works/.alt: Sequence diagram between browser, DNS resolver and web server: the browser asks DNS for the IP address, opens a TCP connection and TLS handshake with the server, sends a GET request, and receives a 200 OK response with HTML

/computer-science/process-vs-thread/.alt: A process box containing shared code, data, heap and open files, with three threads inside, each having its own registers, program counter and stack

/computer-science/rest-api-basics/.alt: A client sends HTTP requests with methods GET, POST, PATCH and DELETE to a REST API server exposing the orders resource; the server reads and writes a database and returns JSON with status codes such as 200, 201, 204 and 404

/computer-science/solid-principles/.alt: Five tiles spelling SOLID: S for single responsibility, O for open closed, L for Liskov substitution, I for interface segregation and D for dependency inversion

/computer-science/sorting-algorithms/.alt: Bottom up merge sort of the array 5, 2, 4, 7, 1, 3, 2, 6: pass 1 merges single items into sorted pairs 2 5, 4 7, 1 3, 2 6; pass 2 merges pairs into 2 4 5 7 and 1 2 3 6; pass 3 merges these into the sorted array 1 2 2 3 4 5 6 7

/computer-science/stack-vs-queue/.alt: Left: a stack of four boxes labelled 10, 20, 30 and 40 from bottom to top, with push and pop arrows both at the top. Right: a queue of four boxes 10, 20, 30, 40 from front to rear, with dequeue at the front on the left and enqueue at the rear on the right.

/computer-science/types-of-software-test.alt: Test pyramid: a wide base of many fast unit tests, a middle layer of fewer integration tests, and a small top of end to end system tests; arrows show that tests higher up are slower and more expensive while lower tests are faster and cheaper

/computer-science/von-neumann-vs-harvard.alt: Left: Von Neumann architecture with a CPU connected by a single bus to one memory that holds both instructions and data. Right: Harvard architecture with a CPU connected by two separate buses to an instruction memory and a data memory

/electrical-engineering/dc-motor-working.alt: Equivalent circuit of a DC shunt motor: a DC supply V feeds a line current IL that splits into a field current If through the shunt field winding and an armature current Ia through armature resistance Ra and the armature, which generates back EMF Eb. Equations V equals Eb plus Ia Ra, Eb equals k phi omega, and T equals k phi Ia are listed.

/electrical-engineering/ohms-law-kirchho.alt: Circuit: 12 V source in series with R1 of 4 ohms, feeding R2 of 6 ohms and R3 of 12 ohms in parallel

/electrical-engineering/power-factor/.alt: Power triangle: real power P horizontal, reactive power Q vertical, apparent power S as the hypotenuse, with angle phi between P and S

/electrical-engineering/thevenins-theore.alt: Left: a 24 volt source with series resistor R1 of 6 ohms, a shunt resistor R2 of 3 ohms, and a series resistor R3 of 2 ohms leading to terminals A and B with load RL. Right: the Thevenin equivalent, a source Vth of 8 volts in series with Rth of 4 ohms feeding the same terminals.

/electrical-engineering/transformer-loss.alt: Single-phase transformer with an AC supply feeding the primary winding on the left limb of a laminated core and a load on the secondary winding on the right limb. Power flows from primary to secondary. Core loss from hysteresis and eddy currents occurs in the core, and copper loss I squared R occurs in the primary and secondary windings.

/electrical-engineering/transformer-work.alt: Single-phase transformer: primary winding with N1 turns on the left limb and secondary winding with N2 turns on the right limb of a laminated core

/electronics-engineering/active-vs-passi.alt: Bode magnitude plot of a first order passive RC low pass filter and a second order active Butterworth low pass filter, both with a 1 kilohertz cutoff. Both are 3 dB down at the cutoff; the first order curve then falls at 20 dB per decade and the second order curve at 40 dB per decade.

/electronics-engineering/buck-converter/.alt: Buck converter: input voltage, series switch, diode from switch node to ground, series inductor, output capacitor and load

/electronics-engineering/cmos-inverter/.alt: CMOS inverter block diagram: PMOS between VDD and output, NMOS between output and ground, both gates connected to the input

/electronics-engineering/inverting-and-n.alt: Inverting amplifier: input through Rin to the inverting input, feedback resistor Rf from output to inverting input, non-inverting input grounded

/electronics-engineering/transistor-work.alt: NPN transistor structure: a wide N type emitter on the left, a thin P type base in the middle and an N type collector on the right. Electrons flow from emitter through base to collector. A small base current leaves at the base terminal. The base emitter junction is forward biased and the base collector junction reverse biased.

/environmental-engineering/activated-slu.alt: Activated sludge process: primary effluent enters the aeration tank with diffusers supplying air bubbles; mixed liquor flows to a circular secondary clarifier; clear effluent leaves over the weir; settled sludge is pumped back as return activated sludge to the aeration tank inlet, and excess sludge is removed as waste activated sludge

/environmental-engineering/cems-overview.alt: Extractive CEMS: a heated probe in the stack withdraws sample gas through a heated line to a sample conditioning unit with a cooler and filter, then to gas analysers in a shelter; a dust monitor and flow monitor are mounted on the stack; all signals go to the data acquisition system and then to the regulator's server

/environmental-engineering/circular-econ.alt: Circular economy loops for a technical product: from design and manufacture to use, then inner to outer loops returning to earlier stages: maintain and repair back to use, reuse and redistribute, refurbish and remanufacture back to manufacture, recycle back to materials; a small residual stream goes to energy recovery or landfill

/environmental-engineering/electrostatic.alt: Plan view of an ESP duct: dirty gas enters from the left between two grounded collection plates; a row of negative discharge wires in the centre produces corona; charged particles migrate sideways to the plates; clean gas exits on the right; dust falls from the plates into hoppers below when rapped

/environmental-engineering/environmental.alt: EIA process flowchart: project proposal, screening with a branch to no EIA required, scoping, baseline studies, impact prediction and evaluation, mitigation and alternatives, EIA report and EMP, public consultation, review and decision, then monitoring and compliance; public consultation links back to the report

/environmental-engineering/life-cycle-as.alt: ISO 14040 LCA framework: goal and scope definition, inventory analysis and impact assessment stacked on the left, each linked by two way arrows to interpretation on the right; direct applications such as product development, policy and marketing shown outside the framework

/environmental-engineering/reverse-osmos.alt: Reverse osmosis process flow. Feed water passes through pretreatment, then a high pressure pump, into a pressure vessel divided by a membrane. Water passes through the membrane to the low pressure permeate side and leaves as product water. The concentrated brine leaves the high pressure side through a control valve.

/environmental-engineering/sewage-treatm.alt: Sewage treatment plant process flow diagram: raw sewage passes through screens, a grit chamber, a primary clarifier, an aeration tank with a surface aerator, a secondary clarifier and a disinfection unit before discharge to the outfall; return activated sludge is pumped from the secondary clarifier back to the aeration tank inlet, and primary sludge and waste activated sludge go to sludge treatment

/environmental-engineering/solid-waste-m.alt: Inverted pyramid of the waste hierarchy from most preferred at the top to least preferred at the bottom: prevention, reuse, recycling, recovery including composting and energy recovery, and disposal

/environmental-engineering/water-treatme.alt: Conventional water treatment train: raw water intake with screen, rapid mix tank with coagulant dosing, flocculation tank with slow paddles, sedimentation tank with sludge withdrawal, sand filter, chlorine contact tank, then clear water storage and distribution

/manufacturing-engineering/3d-printing-t.alt: Three schematics: FDM with filament feeding a heated nozzle depositing a bead onto a build plate; SLA with a UV laser beam curing resin in a vat while the platform lifts the part; SLS with a laser fusing a layer of powder in a powder bed with a recoater roller spreading new powder

/manufacturing-engineering/cnc-machine-w.alt: CNC control loop: CAD and CAM produce G-code loaded into the CNC controller; the controller sends commands to a servo drive and servo motor, which turns a ball screw that moves the machine table on linear guides; an encoder on the motor and a linear scale on the table feed position back to the controller; the spindle with cutting tool machines the workpiece on the table

/manufacturing-engineering/cnc-turning-v.alt: Side by side comparison of CNC turning and CNC milling. Left: in turning the workpiece held in a chuck rotates about the Z axis while a single point tool feeds along Z toward the chuck. Right: in milling a multi-tooth end mill in the spindle rotates while the workpiece clamped on the table feeds horizontally past it.

/manufacturing-engineering/control-chart.alt: X-bar control chart: horizontal axis is sample number from 1 to 20, vertical axis is sample mean; centre line in the middle with upper and lower control limits; most points vary randomly between the limits, but point 16 lies above the upper control limit and is circled as an out of control signal

/manufacturing-engineering/eoq-inventory.alt: Two charts. Left: sawtooth inventory level over time, rising instantly to Q at each order arrival and falling linearly to zero, with average inventory Q over 2 shown as a dashed line and reorder point marked. Right: annual cost versus order quantity, with ordering cost falling, holding cost rising linearly, and total cost a U shaped curve with its minimum at EOQ where the two cost curves cross

/manufacturing-engineering/manufacturing.alt: Tree diagram: manufacturing processes branch into six groups: primary shaping, forming, material removal, joining, additive manufacturing, and property change and finishing, each with example processes listed below

/manufacturing-engineering/metal-casting.alt: Cross-section of a two part sand mould in a flask: cope on top and drag below separated by the parting line, with pouring basin, sprue, runner, gate, casting cavity containing a core, and a riser

/manufacturing-engineering/production-pl.alt: Planning hierarchy from long term to short term: demand forecast and orders feed aggregate planning, then master production schedule, then MRP using bill of materials and inventory records, then capacity planning, then scheduling and dispatching on the shop floor, with feedback from shop floor control back to planning

/manufacturing-engineering/seven-wastes-.alt: Seven circles arranged around a central circle labelled muda, the seven wastes; the outer circles are labelled transport, inventory, motion, waiting, overproduction, overprocessing and defects, with short examples beneath each

/manufacturing-engineering/six-sigma-dma.alt: Five connected chevrons labelled Define, Measure, Analyse, Improve and Control, with key questions under each: what is the problem, how big is it, what causes it, how do we fix it, how do we sustain it

/manufacturing-engineering/time-and-moti.alt: Top view of a workstation: an operator at the bottom edge with left and right hands; inner arcs show the normal working area reachable with forearms, outer arcs show the maximum working area with arms extended; parts bins and tools are placed inside the normal area, assembly fixture in the centre

/manufacturing-engineering/types-of-main.alt: Tree diagram: maintenance divides into corrective maintenance (breakdown, immediate or deferred) and preventive maintenance; preventive divides into predetermined (time based, usage based) and condition based (predictive with monitoring); proactive and RCM sit across both as strategy layers

/marine-engineering/fixed-vs-floating-of.alt: Side by side: left shows fixed structures, a monopile and a jacket, standing on the seabed in shallow water and carrying wind turbines; right shows floating structures in deep water, a semi-submersible with catenary mooring lines and a spar with taut mooring lines, both carrying wind turbines

/marine-engineering/marine-propeller-typ.alt: Marine propeller types diagram: end views from aft of a four blade fixed pitch propeller with blades cast integral with a small hub and a four blade controllable pitch propeller with bolted blades on a larger hub, both turning clockwise for ahead as right-hand propellers; below, a side view of a CPP shaft line showing a hydraulic power unit feeding oil through an oil distribution box and a hollow shaft to a servo piston in the hub, with return oil flowing back, and water accelerated aft by the propeller

/marine-engineering/ship-auxiliary-machi.alt: Disc stack centrifugal purifier cross section: dirty oil enters at the top through the central inlet and flows down to the bottom of the rotating bowl; disc stack in the bowl separates lighter clean oil moving inward to the oil outlet and heavier water moving outward to the water outlet via the gravity disc; solids collect at the bowl periphery and are discharged through sludge ports

/marine-engineering/ship-electrical-powe.alt: Single line diagram of a ship electrical system: three diesel generators and a shaft generator feed a main switchboard with a bus tie; the main switchboard supplies large motors, a 440 to 230 volt transformer for lighting and small power distribution boards, and the emergency switchboard through an interconnector; the emergency generator feeds the emergency switchboard which supplies emergency lighting, communications and fire pump; a shore connection box connects to the main switchboard

/marine-engineering/ship-resistance-and-.alt: Diagram of the ship power chain from engine brake power through shaft power, delivered power and thrust power to effective power, and a breakdown of total resistance into frictional resistance, residuary resistance and air and appendage resistance.

/marine-engineering/ship-stability-basic.alt: Cross section of a ship heeled to starboard: waterline inclined; centre of gravity G on the centreline; centre of buoyancy moved from B to B1 towards the low side; buoyancy force acting upward through B1 crossing the centreline at metacentre M above G; weight acting down through G; horizontal distance GZ between the two lines is the righting lever

/marine-engineering/solas-lifesaving-fir.alt: Side view of a cargo ship showing locations of safety equipment: free-fall lifeboat at the stern, liferafts on each side with hydrostatic release units, rescue boat, lifebuoys along the rails, EPIRB on the bridge top, fire stations and hydrants along the deck, emergency fire pump room, CO2 room, and fixed CO2 system protecting the engine room

/marine-engineering/two-stroke-marine-di.alt: Uniflow scavenged two-stroke cylinder: cylinder cover with central exhaust valve and fuel injectors at the top, piston in the liner, scavenge air ports around the lower liner, scavenge air receiver supplying air, piston rod to crosshead and connecting rod to crankshaft below; arrows show air entering through ports and exhaust leaving through the valve to the turbocharger

/materials-engineering/engineering-mater.alt: Classification tree: engineering materials divide into metals (ferrous and non-ferrous), ceramics and glasses, polymers (thermoplastics, thermosets, elastomers), composites (polymer, metal and ceramic matrix), and advanced materials (semiconductors, biomaterials, smart, nanomaterials)

/materials-engineering/fatigue-failure/.alt: S-N curves on log scale: stress amplitude versus number of cycles from 10 to the 3 to 10 to the 9; a steel curve falls and then becomes horizontal at the endurance limit around 10 to the 6 cycles; an aluminium curve keeps falling without a clear limit

/materials-engineering/heat-treatment-of.alt: Temperature versus time schematic of heat treatments: steel heated above the critical temperature into austenite; annealing cools slowly in the furnace, normalizing cools in air, hardening quenches rapidly to room temperature forming martensite, then tempering reheats to a moderate temperature below the critical line and cools; dashed horizontal line marks the A1 critical temperature at 727 degrees Celsius

/materials-engineering/iron-carbon-phase.alt: Simplified iron-iron carbide phase diagram: temperature from 600 to 1600 degrees Celsius on the vertical axis, carbon content 0 to 6.67 percent on the horizontal axis; regions labelled liquid, austenite gamma, ferrite alpha plus austenite, ferrite plus cementite (pearlite), austenite plus cementite, and liquid plus austenite; eutectoid point at 0.76 percent carbon and 727 degrees, eutectic point at 4.3 percent carbon and 1147 degrees; vertical dashed line at 2.14 percent separates steels and cast irons

/materials-engineering/mechanical-proper.alt: Engineering stress-strain curve for a ductile metal showing the linear elastic region with slope E, the 0.2 percent offset line defining yield strength, strain hardening up to the ultimate tensile strength, necking and fracture, with the area under the elastic part marked as resilience and the total area as toughness

/materials-engineering/ndt-methods/.alt: Pulse echo ultrasonic testing: a probe on the top surface of a steel plate sends a sound pulse down; part reflects from an internal flaw and the rest from the back wall; an A-scan display shows the initial pulse, a flaw echo at a shorter time and a back wall echo at a longer time

/materials-engineering/tensile-test/.alt: Engineering stress-strain curve for mild steel: straight elastic line rising from the origin to the upper yield point, a drop and a flat yield plateau, then strain hardening rising to a maximum at the ultimate tensile strength, followed by necking where stress falls until fracture; labels for elastic region, yield point, strain hardening, UTS, necking and fracture; 0.2 percent offset line illustrated

/materials-engineering/thermoplastics-vs.alt: Left: thermoplastic with separate tangled polymer chains not chemically bonded to each other. Right: thermoset with chains joined by many cross-links forming a rigid three dimensional network

/materials-engineering/types-of-corrosio.alt: Galvanic corrosion cell: a steel plate and a copper plate joined electrically and immersed in seawater; steel is the anode and dissolves releasing iron ions, copper is the cathode where oxygen is reduced; electrons flow through the metallic connection from steel to copper, ions move through the electrolyte

/materials-engineering/types-of-steel/.alt: Classification tree of steel: carbon steels divided into low, medium and high carbon with a carbon content scale from 0 to 1.4 wt% marked at 0.25 and 0.60; alloy steels divided into low alloy and HSLA; stainless steels divided into austenitic, ferritic, martensitic, duplex and precipitation hardening; tool steels divided into water hardening, cold work, hot work, high speed and shock resisting

/materials-engineering/types-of-welding-.alt: Four simplified process sketches: SMAW with flux coated electrode and gas shield from burning flux plus slag; GMAW with a wire fed through a gas nozzle; GTAW with a tungsten electrode in a gas cup and separate filler rod; SAW with wire feeding into a blanket of granular flux covering the arc

/mechanical-engineering/bernoulli-equati.alt: Venturi meter: flow enters a pipe of area A1 at pressure p1, accelerates through a narrow throat of area A2 where pressure p2 is lower, then recovers in a diverging section; two pressure tappings connect to a differential pressure gauge

/mechanical-engineering/carnot-cycle/.alt: Carnot cycle P-V diagram for an ideal gas heat engine: state 1 to 2 isothermal expansion at the hot temperature TH with heat QH added, 2 to 3 adiabatic expansion, 3 to 4 isothermal compression at the cold temperature TL with heat QL rejected, and 4 to 1 adiabatic compression, traced clockwise; the adiabats are steeper than the hyperbolic isotherms and the enclosed area is the net work

/mechanical-engineering/centrifugal-pump.alt: End view of a centrifugal pump: liquid enters the impeller eye at the centre, the clockwise rotating impeller with backward curved vanes throws it into the spiral volute casing, whose area grows towards the discharge nozzle at the top right

/mechanical-engineering/factor-of-safety.alt: Bar chart showing working stress, allowable stress and yield strength, with the factor of safety as the ratio of yield strength to working stress

/mechanical-engineering/finite-element-a.alt: Cantilever beam fixed to a wall on the left, divided into a mesh of rectangular elements with nodes at the corners, and a downward point load at the free end on the right

/mechanical-engineering/laws-of-thermody.alt: Heat engine diagram: heat Qh flows from a hot reservoir at Th into the engine, the engine delivers work W, and rejects heat Qc to a cold reservoir at Tc

/mechanical-engineering/modes-of-heat-tr.alt: Three panels showing conduction through a solid wall from hot to cold side, convection from a hot plate to moving air, and radiation from a hot body to a cold body as waves

/mechanical-engineering/poissons-ratio/.alt: A bar of original length L and diameter d, drawn dashed, is pulled by axial forces F at both ends. The loaded bar, drawn solid, is longer by delta L and thinner by delta d.

/mechanical-engineering/stress-and-strai.alt: Stress strain curve for ductile steel showing the linear elastic region, yield point, strain hardening up to ultimate tensile strength, necking and fracture

/mechanical-engineering/types-of-gears/.alt: Spur gear pair: a 20 tooth driving pinion meshing with a 60 tooth driven gear, showing dashed pitch circles touching at the pitch point, the 20 degree line of action, opposite directions of rotation and the 120 millimetre centre distance.

/mechanical-engineering/types-of-lubrica.alt: Stribeck curve: coefficient of friction is high in the boundary region at low values of viscosity times speed over load, falls through the mixed region to a minimum, then rises slowly in the hydrodynamic region

/mechanical-engineering/vapour-compressi.alt: Vapour compression refrigeration cycle loop: compressor on the right raises pressure, condenser at the top rejects heat to surroundings, expansion valve on the left drops pressure, evaporator at the bottom absorbs heat from the cold space; states 1 to 4 are marked

/mining-engineering/drilling-and-blastin.alt: Bench blast cross section: bench face on the right with free face; two vertical blastholes behind it; each hole has stemming at the top, explosive charge below, and subdrill below the floor level; burden is the distance from the front hole to the free face, spacing between holes; bench height and subdrill dimensions marked

/mining-engineering/froth-flotation/.alt: Mechanical flotation cell: conditioned slurry feed enters the tank; a rotating impeller at the bottom disperses air drawn down a central shaft into fine bubbles; hydrophobic mineral particles attach to bubbles and rise into the froth layer, which overflows the lip into a launder as concentrate; tailings leave from the bottom side

/mining-engineering/mine-hazards-and-con.alt: Inverted triangle hierarchy of controls from most effective at the top to least effective at the bottom: elimination, substitution, engineering controls, administrative controls, personal protective equipment, with mining examples for each

/mining-engineering/mine-ventilation-sys.alt: Mine ventilation circuit: fresh air enters a downcast intake shaft on the left, flows along an intake airway to the working face, where an auxiliary fan and duct ventilate a dead-end heading; contaminated air returns along the return airway to an upcast shaft on the right, where the main exhaust fan at the surface draws it out; a stopping separates intake and return, a door and a regulator control flow

/mining-engineering/mineral-exploration-.alt: Exploration funnel: wide top stage of regional target generation with remote sensing and data review, then reconnaissance mapping and geochemistry, then geophysics and detailed mapping, then drilling, then resource estimation; cost per area increases and the number of targets decreases down the funnel

/mining-engineering/mining-explosives-ty.alt: Cross section of a loaded mining blasthole: crushed rock stemming at the top, a column charge of ANFO or emulsion below it, and a primer made of a cast booster with a detonator near the bottom; a shock tube downline runs from a surface connector down the hole to the detonator, and the detonation front travels upward from the primer through the column charge

/mining-engineering/open-pit-mine-design.alt: Cross-section of an open pit wall showing four benches with a haul ramp between the second and third bench, labels for bench height, bench face angle, catch berm, ramp, crest, toe, inter-ramp angle and overall slope angle

/mining-engineering/rock-mass-classifica.alt: Drill core run 1.5 m long shown as a row of core pieces of different lengths; pieces 100 mm or longer are shaded and counted towards RQD, shorter pieces are left white

/mining-engineering/surface-vs-undergrou.alt: Cross section comparison. Left: open pit mine with stepped benches cut into the ground to reach a shallow orebody, waste dump beside it. Right: underground mine with a vertical shaft and headframe, horizontal levels and stopes reaching a deep orebody, with a small surface footprint

/petroleum-engineering/artificial-lift-m.alt: Three wells side by side: a sucker rod pump with a surface pump jack and a downhole plunger pump; an electrical submersible pump with a surface drive, power cable and downhole motor and pump; a gas lift well with gas injected down the annulus entering the tubing through gas lift valves

/petroleum-engineering/crude-oil-distill.alt: Atmospheric crude distillation column: crude from furnace enters near the bottom; products drawn from top to bottom are gas and naphtha at about 30 to 180 degrees Celsius, kerosene 150 to 250, diesel 230 to 350, and atmospheric residue above 350 degrees Celsius at the bottom, which goes to the vacuum column

/petroleum-engineering/drilling-fluid-ty.alt: Drilling fluid circulation: the mud pump draws mud from the mud pits and sends it through the standpipe to the top drive, down inside the drill pipe and out through the bit nozzles; mud and cuttings rise up the annulus between the pipe and the borehole wall, leave through the flow line to the shale shaker, which removes cuttings, and return to the mud pits; a filter cake lines the borehole wall

/petroleum-engineering/lng-process/.alt: LNG value chain as connected blocks: gas field, pretreatment, liquefaction at minus 162 degrees Celsius, storage tank, LNG carrier ship, receiving terminal with regasification, then pipeline grid

/petroleum-engineering/offshore-platform.alt: Offshore platform types arranged by increasing water depth from left to right: jack-up and fixed jacket in shallow water, compliant tower, tension leg platform with vertical tendons, spar with a tall cylindrical hull and catenary moorings, and FPSO ship with turret moorings; seabed slopes down to the right

/petroleum-engineering/pipeline-pigging/.alt: Pigging system: a pig launcher with a closure door and kicker line at the left, the pipeline in the middle with a pig travelling with the flow, and a pig receiver with a closure door at the right; isolation valves at both ends and pig signallers along the line

/petroleum-engineering/porosity-and-perm.alt: Two rock cores. Left: well sorted large grains with large connected pores, high porosity and high permeability, with flow arrows passing through easily. Right: tightly cemented small grains with isolated small pores, low permeability, flow arrows blocked

/petroleum-engineering/reservoir-drive-m.alt: Cross-section of an anticline reservoir. A gas cap sits at the crest above the gas oil contact, the oil zone lies below it, and water fills the flanks below the oil water contact. Arrows show aquifer water moving up dip into the oil zone and gas cap gas expanding downward. A producing well penetrates the oil zone.

/petroleum-engineering/rotary-drilling-r.alt: Rotary drilling rig schematic: derrick with crown block at the top, travelling block and top drive below it, drill line from the drawworks, drill floor, blowout preventer below the floor, wellbore with drill string and bit; mud pump sends mud through the standpipe into the drill string, mud returns up the annulus to the shale shaker and mud tank

/petroleum-engineering/well-logging-meth.alt: Simplified log display with three tracks against depth: gamma ray track shows high readings in shale and low readings in sand; resistivity track shows high resistivity in the upper oil bearing sand and low resistivity in the lower water bearing sand; density and neutron porosity track shows crossover in the gas or porous zone

/renewable-energy/battery-energy-storage.alt: BESS architecture: battery racks made of modules and cells, each with BMS, connect on the DC side to the power conversion system; the PCS connects through a transformer to the grid; the energy management system communicates with BMS, PCS and the grid operator; thermal management and fire suppression support the battery container

/renewable-energy/energy-audit-steps/.alt: Energy audit steps as a sequence of seven boxes: plan and collect data, analyse bills and baseline, site survey and measurement, identify measures, evaluate savings and payback, report, implement and verify; a feedback arrow returns from verify to plan for continuous improvement

/renewable-energy/ev-charging-levels-and.alt: Five connector faces drawn schematically: Type 1 round with five pins, Type 2 with flat top edge and seven pins, CCS2 combining a Type 2 upper part with two large DC pins below, CHAdeMO large round with ten pins, and NACS compact with two large and three small pins

/renewable-energy/green-hydrogen-electro.alt: PEM electrolyser cell: a DC power supply connects to an anode on the left and a cathode on the right separated by a proton exchange membrane; water enters at the anode, oxygen leaves the anode, protons cross the membrane, electrons flow through the external circuit, and hydrogen leaves the cathode

/renewable-energy/how-solar-pv-systems-w.alt: Grid-tied solar PV system: sunlight falls on PV panels producing DC, which passes through a DC isolator to an inverter producing AC, then through an AC distribution board to building loads and a bidirectional meter connected to the utility grid; an optional battery connects to the inverter

/renewable-energy/how-wind-turbines-work.alt: Wind turbine cutaway: three blades attached to a hub, the low speed shaft enters the nacelle to a gearbox, then a high speed shaft drives the generator; a controller, yaw drive and anemometer are on the nacelle; the tower carries power cables down to a transformer at the base

/renewable-energy/microgrid-explained/.alt: Microgrid single line: utility grid connects through a point of common coupling switch to a microgrid AC bus; connected to the bus are solar PV with inverter, battery storage with grid forming inverter, a diesel or gas generator, critical loads and non-critical loads; a microgrid controller communicates with all components

/renewable-energy/solar-inverter-types/.alt: Three architectures: string inverter with panels in series feeding one inverter; microinverters with a small inverter behind each panel feeding an AC bus; central inverter with many strings combined in a combiner box feeding one large inverter

/renewable-energy/solar-panel-efficiency.alt: Left: sunlight of irradiance G falls on a module of area A and the module delivers maximum power Pmax, so efficiency equals Pmax divided by G times A. Right: a graph of relative maximum power against cell temperature, falling from 100 percent at 25 degrees Celsius to about 82.5 percent at 75 degrees, with 89.5 percent marked at 55 degrees.

/renewable-energy/wind-turbine-power-cur.alt: Wind turbine power curve: power as a percentage of rated power against hub height wind speed from 0 to 30 m/s. Output is zero below cut-in at 3 m/s (Region 1), rises roughly with the cube of wind speed to rated power at about 12 m/s (Region 2), stays flat at rated power under pitch control up to cut-out at 25 m/s (Region 3), then drops to zero with the turbine stopped (Region 4)

/safety-engineering/fire-classes-and-ext.alt: Fire triangle with sides labelled heat, fuel and oxygen, and a central label chain reaction for the fire tetrahedron; arrows indicate cooling removes heat, starving removes fuel and smothering removes oxygen

/safety-engineering/fmea-explained/.alt: FMEA flow from left to right: function or process step, failure mode, effect rated by severity, cause rated by occurrence, current controls rated by detection, RPN or action priority, recommended actions, then re-rating after actions

/safety-engineering/hazop-study/.alt: HAZOP loop: select node, describe design intent, select parameter, apply guide word to form a deviation, identify causes, consequences and safeguards, record recommendations; repeat for all guide words, all parameters and all nodes

/safety-engineering/job-safety-analysis/.alt: Flow chart of the job safety analysis steps: select the job, involve workers, break the job into steps, identify hazards for each step, decide controls using the hierarchy of controls, document and communicate, then review and update with a feedback arrow back to the job steps

/safety-engineering/lopa-explained/.alt: LOPA event path: an initiating event on the left produces a frequency arrow that passes through five independent protection layers in turn, BPCS, alarm and operator response, SIF, relief device and dike, becoming thinner after each layer until a much reduced frequency reaches the consequence on the right

/safety-engineering/mtbf-mttr-availabili.alt: Bathtub curve of failure rate versus time: high but decreasing failure rate during early life (infant mortality), low constant failure rate during useful life where MTBF applies, and rising failure rate during wear-out

/safety-engineering/risk-matrix/.alt: 5 by 5 risk matrix: likelihood 1 to 5 on the vertical axis, severity 1 to 5 on the horizontal axis, cells contain the product score from 1 to 25 and are coloured green for low, yellow for medium, orange for high and red for extreme

/safety-engineering/root-cause-analysis-.alt: Fishbone diagram: a horizontal spine leads to the problem box at the right labelled pump bearing failure; six angled bones labelled man, machine and method above, and material, measurement and environment below, each with example causes

/safety-engineering/safety-integrity-lev.alt: Safety instrumented function: a pressure transmitter on a vessel sends a signal to a safety PLC logic solver, which commands a solenoid and shutdown valve on the inlet line to close; the SIL of the function depends on the reliability of all three parts combined

/safety-engineering/types-of-fire-detect.alt: Fire development curve over time from incipient to smouldering to flaming to intense heat stages, with markers showing that aspirating smoke detectors respond earliest, then point smoke detectors, then flame detectors when flames appear, and heat detectors last

/telecommunication-engineering/5g-networ.alt: 5G architecture: user equipment connects by radio to gNB base stations in the radio access network; the gNBs connect to the 5G core, where control plane functions AMF, SMF, PCF, UDM and AUSF sit on a service bus, and the UPF forwards user data to edge applications and the internet

/telecommunication-engineering/firewalls.alt: Firewall between an untrusted network on the left and a trusted network on the right, with a DMZ below; traffic arrows pass through a rule table, permitted traffic continues, denied traffic is dropped

/telecommunication-engineering/geo-meo-l.alt: Earth at the left with three orbit arcs at increasing distance: LEO close to Earth at about 160 to 2000 km, MEO further at about 2000 to 35786 km, and GEO furthest at 35786 km; each with a satellite and a coverage cone, wider for higher orbits

/telecommunication-engineering/ip-addres.alt: The address 192.168.10.77 with prefix /26 shown as four binary octets. The first 26 bits form the network portion and the last 6 bits the host portion. Below, the 192.168.10.0/24 block is divided into four /26 subnets starting at .0, .64, .128 and .192, with the .64 subnet highlighted because it contains .77.

/telecommunication-engineering/modulatio.alt: Four stacked waveforms: a digital bit stream 1 0 1 1 0; ASK with carrier present for ones and absent for zeros; FSK with higher frequency for ones and lower for zeros; BPSK with carrier phase reversed for zeros

/telecommunication-engineering/osi-vs-tc.alt: Side by side mapping: OSI layers 7 application, 6 presentation and 5 session map to the TCP/IP application layer; OSI layer 4 transport maps to transport; OSI layer 3 network maps to internet; OSI layers 2 data link and 1 physical map to link layer. Example protocols are listed on the right

/telecommunication-engineering/router-vs.alt: Network with a router in the centre connecting the internet above to two switches below; switch A connects office PCs on network 192.168.10.0/24, switch B connects a PLC and HMI on network 192.168.20.0/24

/telecommunication-engineering/single-mo.alt: Two fibre cross sections. Top: multimode fibre with a wide core and several light rays following curved paths of different lengths. Bottom: single-mode fibre with a narrow core and a single straight light path along the axis

/telecommunication-engineering/vlan-expl.alt: Two switches joined by an 802.1Q trunk carrying VLAN 10 and VLAN 20; PC1 and PC3 are on VLAN 10 access ports, PC2 and PC4 on VLAN 20 access ports; below, an Ethernet frame with the 4 byte 802.1Q tag between the source MAC address and the type field, the tag made of TPID 0x8100, PCP 3 bits, DEI 1 bit and VLAN ID 12 bits

/telecommunication-engineering/wi-fi-sta.alt: 2.4 GHz band showing overlapping 20 MHz channels, with channels 1, 6 and 11 highlighted as non-overlapping arcs; a note that 5 GHz and 6 GHz bands provide many more non-overlapping channels
